introduction: With the outbreak of World War II in 1939, the Indian freedom struggle entered its final and most decisive phase. The British dragged India into the war without consulting its leaders, prompting the Congress provincial ministries to resign. This era was marked by the 'Quit India Movement' and Netaji's military campaigns, ultimately leading to India's independence in 1947.

core_concepts.title: Cripps Mission (1942)
core_concepts.description: The British government sent Sir Stafford Cripps to India to secure full Indian cooperation for their war efforts, promising 'Dominion Status' after the war. Both Congress and the Muslim League rejected it.

core_concepts.title: Quit India Movement (1942)
core_concepts.description: On August 8, 1942, Mahatma Gandhi launched the 'Quit India Movement' from Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay, giving the famous slogan 'Do or Die'.

core_concepts.title: Indian National Army (INA)
core_concepts.description: Subhas Chandra Bose reorganized the Indian National Army during WWII to free India from British rule through military struggle, giving slogans like 'Delhi Chalo' and 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom'.

core_concepts.title: Cabinet Mission (1946)
core_concepts.description: A delegation of three British cabinet ministers arrived to negotiate the transfer of power. They proposed the formation of a Constituent Assembly to frame India's constitution.

core_concepts.title: Mountbatten Plan (1947)
core_concepts.description: On June 3, 1947, Lord Mountbatten proposed the partition of British India into two independent dominions (India and Pakistan). It was accepted, leading to independence on August 15, 1947.

important_entities.name: Mahatma Gandhi
important_entities.significance: Led the 1942 movement, though he was arrested immediately and imprisoned in the Aga Khan Palace.

important_entities.name: Subhas Chandra Bose
important_entities.significance: Made the most robust attempt to gain independence through armed struggle from outside India.

important_entities.name: Lord Mountbatten
important_entities.significance: Became the first Governor-General of independent India and executed the transfer of power.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse these two. The Cripps Mission (1942) came during the war offering 'Dominion Status', while the Cabinet Mission (1946) came after the war to form the Constituent Assembly.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Origin of the 'Do or Die' slogan
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While Gandhi popularized it, the slogans 'Quit India' and 'Do or Die' were originally coined by Yusuf Meherally (who also coined 'Simon Go Back').

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: An easy way to remember the sequence: Cripps Mission (1942) -> Quit India Movement (1942) -> Cabinet Mission (1946).

exam_strategy_tips: Questions often ask where the Quit India resolution was passed (Answer: Wardha session / Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay).
Remember that the 'Mountbatten Plan' is also known as the 'June 3rd Plan'.
